newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex fends off Dow bears to boost Mexican stocks.
newsitem.headline: Telmex fends off Dow bears to boost Mexican stocks.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed up on Tuesday despite sluggish Dow industrials as market heavyweight Telmex chalked up gains in New York and Mexico, traders said.
"Telmex prices were several days behind the Dow Jones. Today they took off and headed for the $33 mark," a floor trader said
Telmex series L shares closed 36 centavos (5 cents) higher at 12.34 pesos ($1.65) in Mexico, while its ADRs gained 1/2 to $33 in New York.
The bolsa's leading IPC index, in which Telmex has the heaviest weighting, closed 42.18 points, or 1.27 percent, at 3,353.79.
Analysts said Telmex was boosted by the brokerage HSBC James Capel upgrading the stock from hold to long-term buy.
The Dow Jones meanwhile closed down 0.37 point, or 0.01 percent, at 5,888.83.
Despite today's gains in Mexico, some technical analysts felt the market has yet to reach volume levels needed to spur a rally. Volume was mediocre at 71.3 million shares.

"There's no chance of a rally in the short term as long as trade is this dull and we stay in a stabilisation period with the IPC moving in a band between 3,250 and 3,360 points," said a technical analyst.

Another factor shoring up the Bolsa, traders said, was market expectation that interest rates would fall at Tuesday's primary auction. A Reuters survey of money market traders showed they expected the benchmark 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bill, rate to fall by 0.23 percentage points to 23.23 percent.

A total of 109 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered losers by 55 to 24, with the remaining 30 unchanged. Mining company Penoles headed the gainers, closing 1.60 pesos (21 cents) up at 33.20 pesos ($4.43), followed by brewers Grupo Modelo which closed 1.85 pesos (25 cents) up at 39.25 pesos ($5.23).
Traders said Modelo was boosted by London-based brokerage Kleinwort Benson recommending a long-term buy for the stock.
